short.q: Describe the structure of Paper 2 and how many marks each section is worth.
short.model: Paper 2 lasts 1 h 45 min and has Section A, reading, five passages for 40 marks, and Section B, writing and grammar (Q6, Q7, Q8), for 40 marks.
points: Section A reading, five passages, 40 marks
Section B writing and grammar (Q6, Q7, Q8), 40 marks

short.q: Explain how Speaking Tasks B and C are different from Task A.
short.model: Task A is about your own chosen picture with five questions; B and C are spontaneous conversations on two different themes chosen at random by Pearson, so you cannot rely on a prepared speech.
points: Task A: own picture, five questions
B and C: spontaneous, different themes chosen at random

short.q: Give three ways to avoid losing marks in Q7.
short.model: Address every bullet point, use a range of tenses with opinions and reasons, and stay within 130–150 words while checking verb position and endings.
points: Past, present and future plus opinions with reasons
Keep to word count and check accuracy

short.q: A listening speaker says 'Eigentlich wollte ich ins Kino gehen, aber jetzt gehe ich schwimmen.' What is the answer to 'what will he do?' and why?
short.model: He will go swimming. The speaker changed his mind: the first thing mentioned (cinema) was the original plan, not the final one.
points: Cinema was the original plan, replaced after 'aber'

short.q: Why must you read the word in brackets in Q8 in context?
short.model: The word does not always change; you must check the subject, tense, case and gender of the sentence to decide the correct form.
points: Sometimes the word stays the same
